deepDiveThesesUsed.summary: Apps advertise '60+ supported models' but the vendored llama.cpp build only recognizes specific LLM_ARCH_* tags, so many trending releases (e.g. Qwen3.x) silently can't load.

The GGUF quant label (e.g. Q4_K_M) is not a standardized artifact — different quantizers (and even a vendor's own official QAT release) produce measurably different quality/size under the identical nominal tag.

The app's July 10 Swift rewrite fixed the July 7 staleness gap by fetching llama.cpp's latest GitHub release at build time instead of a pinned old commit, but that fetch resolves 'latest' fresh every build with no pinned tag and no version ever surfaced to the user, so two builds cut hours or days apart can silently embed different sets of supported architectures with no way to tell which one shipped. Backed by real llama.cpp release-cadence data (3 tags in under 3 hours) and PR merge-time data (~1 day to 24 days depending on whether an architecture is genuinely new). Adjacent to but distinct from the 07-07 thesis: static staleness vs. dynamic non-determinism.

PrismML's launch post for Bonsai 27B (a ternary/1-bit quantized Qwen3.6-27B) calls it 'the first model of its capability class to run on a phone.' Its own Hugging Face model card for the high-quality Ternary variant states the build's ~7.2 GB deployed footprint 'exceeds the ~6 GB per-app iOS memory budget' PrismML's own launch post defines for a 12 GB iPhone -- 1.2 GB over. The variant that does fit inside that budget (1-bit, 3.9 GB) retains only 89.5% of FP16 quality overall, with tool-calling dropping 17.5% relative (80.00 -> 66.03, BFCL v3/tau-squared-Bench) and vision 18.0% relative (72.61 -> 59.57). Corroborated independently by top comments on the model's 680-point Hacker News launch thread. NOTE FOR REVIEWERS: a same-week run (2026-07-15, see the 2026-07-15 note below, state carried on then-unmerged PR #23 / branch claude/brave-brown-142mf8) researched the SAME underlying model and explored a DIFFERENT specific angle (the 89.5% headline average hiding a steeper 74.0% retention specifically on tau-squared-Bench) and ran that angle through 6 Blotato-graded hook iterations that plateaued at 7-8/10 and were correctly not published. This piece uses a different core fact (the vendor's own memory-budget arithmetic not adding up, not a benchmark-composition critique) and a title rewritten specifically to lead with the sharpest number in sentence one, which the prior attempt's own rubric flagged as a requirement its titles were failing. Self-graded 9/10 in this session (no /post-grader skill and no Blotato access available) after two honest title iterations -- flagging this origin story plainly so a human editor can double-check this call given the adjacent thesis's plateau, rather than silently treating it as a first attempt.

CRITICAL GAP: the new native engine is NOT version-pinned. scripts/fetch-llama.sh always downloads whatever is the LATEST ggml-org/llama.cpp GitHub release at build time — no tag/commit is recorded anywhere in the repo, the resulting Frameworks/llama.xcframework is gitignored (not committed), there is no CI that would capture which version went into any given build, and no App Store release/tag exists yet for the native app (README still self-describes as 'Phase 0 — engine spike', which is itself stale given Phases 1-4 already merged). This means there is currently NO reliable, checkable source of truth for which GGUF architectures the shipping engine supports — the ENGINE COMPATIBILITY hard gate (quality bar #5) cannot be verified against a stable reference. Until fetch-llama.sh is pinned to an explicit tag/commit (recorded in-repo) or a real App Store release ships with recorded engine version, catalog-compatibility checks in this routine are working from the OLD flutter-legacy llm_arch enum as the conservative fallback, since it's the only fixed, inspectable reference and it's plausible some live installs are still running that build.
